The pMUS preconditioner applies a V-cycle with Gauss-Seidel smoothing starting from the highest polynomial order level down to the lowest order Whitney element level.
The lowest order Whitney system is solved exactly by direct factorization or approximately by incomplete Cholesky factors.
Auxiliary Space Preconditioning transfers the vector field to scalar auxiliary spaces where scalar AMG is applied.
The method uses hierarchical tetrahedral finite elements with up to 4th order basis functions, adding 6, 14, 25, and 39 basis functions for orders 1 to 4 respectively.
Deflation incorporates eigenvectors corresponding to slow-converging modes to accelerate Krylov solver convergence.
MINRES is used for the first adaptive step; deflated COCG is used for subsequent steps.
Eigenvectors for deflation are computed using a harmonic projection method applied to the multilevel preconditioned system.
The largest matrix solved had over 12 million rows and 0.6 billion nonzero entries.
Numerical experiments include a five-resonator iris filter at 3.63 GHz, a split-ring resonator waveguide, a buckyball metallic frame, and a frequency selective surface.
The Krylov solvers terminate when the residual norm is reduced by a factor of 10^-6.
Deflation with 50% of the number of Krylov steps as eigenvectors reduces iteration counts by roughly half in tested cases.
The frequency shift parameter used in the preconditioner is 0.01.
The multilevel cycle uses 2 AMG coarse levels for the ASP part.
The method achieves significant CPU time savings compared to incomplete LU and full LU preconditioners.
The method supports mixed polynomial orders in the mesh, enabling local p-adaption.
The preconditioner preserves symmetry by applying backward and forward Gauss-Seidel in a symmetric pattern.
The deflated Lanczos algorithm is adapted for complex symmetric matrices by replacing Hermitian transpose with simple transpose.
The method is implemented and tested in Matlab on a 64-bit, 4-core Intel processor with 16 GB RAM.
The multilevel preconditioner is applied recursively down to the smallest auxiliary space matrix, which is solved by factorization.
The approach is effective for both free-space and enclosed electromagnetic scattering problems with various boundary conditions.
